needAdmin: Changing the configuration needs an administrator account.
systemManaged: Managed by the system (systemd-networkd). LordOS shows it but does not change it. If you hand it over to LordOS, the system stops configuring it: only do this if it is not the connection you use to manage this computer remotely.
vpn.certBody: {name}: LordOS couldn't confirm who this server is. Often the server is sending an incomplete certificate chain (its own certificate without the intermediate one), which some other systems complete on their own. Trust it only if the fingerprint matches the one your organization gives you.
vpn.certChangedBody: {name}: the server now shows a different certificate from the one you trusted. That happens when a certificate is renewed, but it can also mean another server is posing as it. Trust the new one only if your organization confirms the fingerprint.
vpn.certNeedAdmin: An administrator has to trust this certificate.
vpn.certTitle: This server's certificate couldn't be verified
vpn.enableHint: {name} is optional and not installed. Enabling it installs the free Debian client ({pkg}) with the LordOS package engine. Nothing from Cisco or Fortinet is installed.
vpn.field.routes: Networks through the VPN (empty: all traffic)
vpn.importHint: Pick the file your provider gave you: a WireGuard .conf or an OpenVPN .ovpn (its certificates are read from the same folder). Keys are stored for root only and the interface never sees them again.
vpn.name: Name
vpn.noFiles: No .conf or .ovpn files in your home, Downloads, Documents or Desktop folders.
vpn.none: No VPNs configured. Add one: WireGuard or OpenVPN from its file, or IPsec, PPTP, AnyConnect or Fortinet with its details.
vpn.pptpWarning: PPTP is obsolete and insecure (MS-CHAPv2 and MPPE are easy to break). Only use it if the server offers nothing else.
vpn.ssoHint: Single sign-on (the organization's sign-in page): connecting opens that page in your browser. Sign in there, approving with your authenticator app if it asks, and the VPN connects when you finish. Leave the return port empty unless your organization gives you one (8020 by default).
vpn.ssoNoBrowser: There's no web browser to open the sign-in page. Install one from the Store (or choose one in Settings → Default Apps) and try again.
vpn.ssoOpenBody: {name} is waiting for you to sign in. Open the sign-in page and finish there; the VPN connects on its own.
vpn.ssoWaitBody: {name}: the sign-in page is open in your browser. Finish signing in there and the VPN connects on its own.
vpn.ssoWaitTitle: Waiting for you to sign in on the organization's page…
vpnInterface: This is a VPN interface: manage it from VPN.
wifi.noSae: This network requires WPA3 and the adapter does not support it.
wifi.none: This computer has no Wi-Fi adapter.
